  source (`option` / `env` / `dsh-model` / `path`) are recorded in the Run's
  `run.started` and durable `dsh.run.started` events.
- **Review budget** — 45 min / 2,700,000 ms; `RELAY_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides.

## Pipeline and where it lives

```
implement ──Run submit──▶ verify ──checks──▶ review ──FIX──▶ implement (attempt+1)
   ▲  real dsh headless        Relay runs            │            same worktree,
   │  in the Task worktree     required checks       │            fresh Run
   │                                                 └── IMPLEMENT failed (repairable) ──┐
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        review ──PASS──▶ integration ──submit──▶ merge_ready
                                                                                  (read-only gate)
```

| step | module | reuse |
| -- | -- | -- |
| worktree + disposable Run + brief | `src/run-lifecycle.ts` (ISH-760) | unchanged |
| Run process + JSONL evidence + structured submission | `src/dsh-runner.ts` (ISH-803/810) | unchanged |
| mechanical VERIFY (HEAD-bound, required checks) | `src/verify.ts` + `runMechanicalVerification` (ISH-759) | unchanged |
| **independent headless Claude review** | **`src/reviewer-runner.ts`** (new) | records via `recordReview` |
| **whole-Task sequencing** | **`src/factory.ts`** (new) | reuses the phase machine |
| read-only HEAD-bound merge gate | `src/merge-gate.ts` (ISH-761) | unchanged |

The Factory is **sequencing only**: every transition is the ordinary durable
result (`acceptRunSubmission`, `runMechanicalVerification`, `recordReview`,
`submitPhase`). There is no parallel state machine.

## Bounded IMPLEMENT recovery (ISH-1012)

VERIFY FAIL and REVIEW FIX already continue the Task at `attempt+1`. Before
ISH-1012 an IMPLEMENT Run failure **stopped** the Task
(`coding_failed`/`no_implementation`) with no bounded rework. The Factory now
classifies the failed Run with a small, conservative policy
(`src/implement-recovery.ts`) and, **only when it is provably safe**, issues a
fresh disposable Run on the SAME Task/worktree through the ordinary
phase/attempt transition (`workflow.recordImplementRecovery`):

| failed IMPLEMENT Run | decision |
| -- | -- |
| `exit 0` + **no new commit** (`NO_IMPLEMENTATION`) | **RETRY** (missing-commit) |
| non-zero exit **after producing a new commit** (host worktree) | **RETRY** (partial-commit) |
| the SAME missing-commit/partial-commit at the SAME base HEAD again | **STOP** (`REPEATED_FAILURE`) — no progress, no loop |
| `attempt + 1 >= maxAttempts` | **STOP** (`max_attempts`) — the SAME budget as VERIFY/REVIEW FIX |
| ENOSPC / resource exhaustion (`ENOSPC`/`RESOURCE`) | **BLOCKED**, never retried |
| permission / auth / credential (`PERMISSION`/`AUTH`) | **BLOCKED**, never retried |
| launch problem (`LAUNCH`) | **BLOCKED**, never retried |
| invalid/stale submission (`INVALID_RESULT`) | **BLOCKED**, never retried |
| cancelled / time-limited / unknown cause (`CANCELLED`/`TIMEOUT`/`UNKNOWN_CAUSE`) | **STOPPED**, never retried |
| an unconfirmed live writer (`WRITER_NOT_TERMINAL`) | the fence is held; no new Run |
| the adopted/orphaned Run path (`ORPHAN`) | **STOPPED**; ISH-1008 owns liveness/cause |

The transition is conditional and only runs after the previous Run is
**provably terminal**, no live Run owns `(task, implement, attempt)`, and the
single-writer fence is released for the Run's worktree/branch. A stale/replayed
call therefore observes 0 changes (`STALE_ATTEMPT`) instead of bumping the
attempt twice.

The fresh Run receives the failed Run's id, terminal state/exit code, base and
produced HEAD, its recorded error and a bounded stderr tail, plus the retry
reason, pinned into the SAME Run brief — the original Task acceptance and the
durable worktree are unchanged. A terminal Run **closes** its attempt: restart/
re-entry finishes a clean unsubmitted submission through the normal fence or
re-reads the recorded failure, and **never starts a second Run for that
attempt**. A `blocked_human` HOLD is never bypassed by an in-flight Run.

An environment-class failure parks the Task `blocked_human` at `attempt+1`, so an
explicit `unblock` starts a fresh attempt after the environment is fixed; it is
not an automatic retry.

## Transient provider/network recovery (ISH-1174)

A short outage must not end the lane. `src/transient-failure.ts` classifies a
terminal dsh Run from its EXISTING evidence (the Run row, its `dsh.jsonl` and
stderr): a provider HTTP **5xx** or **429** (a structured `status`/`statusCode`
on the failed `turn_end`, or a code such as `HTTP_500`), a `turn_end
reason=error` code (`TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`, `SERVER`, `RATE_LIMIT`, or a raw
connection code such as `ECONNRESET`/`ECONNREFUSED`), the same `dsh: <CODE>:`
line on stderr, or a connection/network error (timeout, DNS, socket) is
**transient**. The terminal `dsh.run.*` event's `dsh.status` is the COUNT of
status events — never an HTTP status — so it is not read by the classifier.
Auth, permission, ENOSPC/other resource exhaustion, cancellation and genuinely
unknown failures stay non-transient and keep the ISH-1012 policy above. The same
evidence rule applies to a `REVIEW_PROCESS_FAILED` reviewer process: its stderr,
or the structured `claude --output-format json` error envelope (`type:"result"`,
`is_error:true`, with `result` / `api_error_status`) on stdout — never free-text
stdout.

| step | behaviour | evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| wait | provider reachability probe, 30 s doubling to 5 min, TOTAL 60 min | `factory.waiting_transient`; `src/transient-recovery.ts` |
| resume | SAME worktree, `dsh --profile headless --json --session-id <failed id> <short continue prompt>` | `factory.run_resumed` (`runId`, `fromRunId`, `sessionId`, `cause`, `resumeCount`); `src/dsh-runner.ts` |
| attempt budget | a resume does NOT consume a factory attempt; cap **3 resumes per attempt** | `runs.resumed_from_run_id` / `runs.resume_count`; `tests/factory.test.ts` |
| fallback | an unknown/corrupt/missing Session starts a FRESH session in the SAME worktree with the previous final text, `git status` and a diff summary; the adoption check applies only to a session-mode resume (a Run that passed `--session-id`), and auth/ENOSPC/permission never resume — even when the message says "session expired" | `buildFreshSessionResumePrompt`; `classifyUnadoptableSession`; `tests/factory.test.ts` |
| reviewer | a transient `REVIEW_PROCESS_FAILED` is re-run at the SAME head, capped | `factory.review_resumed`; `tests/factory.test.ts` |
| safety | the stale-head fence re-checks the worktree branch/HEAD (and Task head) before any resume; cancel/timeout is never resumed | `checkResumeFence`; `tests/factory.test.ts` |

Caps: `--max-resumes N` (default 3), `--transient-wait DUR` (default 60m),
`--transient-backoff DUR` (default 30s); env `RELAY_TRANSIENT_MAX_RESUMES`,
`RELAY_TRANSIENT_WAIT_MS`, `RELAY_TRANSIENT_BACKOFF_MS`,
`RELAY_TRANSIENT_MAX_BACKOFF_MS`, `RELAY_PROVIDER_PROBE_URL`. On wait/cap
expiry the Factory falls back to the ordinary ISH-1012 stop (never an unbounded
resume loop).

A non-ready Factory result now carries a `failure` projection derived **only**

finished Task (`done`/`failed`/`cancelled`) is not a new failure: it records no
new `factory.outcome` event, so the success or diagnosis that actually ended the

`CHECK_NOT_RUN` is decided from the structured `VerificationResult` row (a
REQUIRED check with `not_run`/`inconclusive`), **before** any process-marker

which may legitimately contain words like `command not found`, `permission

a launch/permission/stale cause.

# ISH-1087 — Factory PR + head-pinned review contract

Status: implemented in Relay (this repo). The ishiul-side Gateway/skill edit is a
separate PR; this document is the contract Relay now enforces.

## The failure this closes

The live ishiul Factory intake records a Task with **no `pr_repo` / `pr_url`** —
only a branch. The old Factory:

- skipped the read-only Task↔PR bind (`if (task.pr_repo || task.pr_url)`), so the
  dsh worker was never told to open a PR;
- ran the reviewer as a **local structured verdict** with no GitHub review;
- reached `merge_ready` with the merge gate `BLOCKED / NO_PR`;
- and credited `TaskMerged` for a merge with **no bound PR at all**.

Evidence: ishiul `T243` / PR #928 and `T238` / PR #916. In the ishiul state DB the
Runs and ReviewResults exist, the Tasks have `pr_url = NULL`, and the merge gate
event is `BLOCKED: CHECKS_NOT_RUN+NO_PERMISSION+NO_PR` (recorded before ISH-1140;
`CHECKS_NOT_RUN` no longer exists as a block reason — see
[`ish-1140-merge-gate.md`](ish-1140-merge-gate.md)). The PR was created only at
merge time by the Gateway.

## Who opens the PR

The **dsh coding worker** does, before its Run ends. The Gateway must not open a
PR except as a recorded fallback.

The Relay Run brief (pinned at `.relay/run-brief.md` and passed as the dsh prompt)
now includes a mandatory section when a GitHub target is resolvable:

- push the Task branch: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` (never the
  default branch);
- open the PR with title **`ISH-<n>: <what changed>`**;
- body follows the target repo's `.github/pull_request_template.md` and includes
  a **`## Documentation Impact`** section (`None` is a valid value);
- on a FIX, push the new commit to the **same** PR and update its body — no
  duplicate;
- never merge and never post a review.

The target repo is the Task's `pr_repo`/`pr_url`, else the Task workspace's
`origin`, else the Factory source checkout (`--pr-repo` overrides). This is why a
Task that records only a branch now gets the instruction.

## What the Factory enforces

1. At intake it records the resolved `pr_repo` on the Task.
2. Before the review stage it **always** runs the read-only bind (when a GitHub
   reader is configured). The PR must be open and its live head must equal the
   produced commit. No PR / moved head / fork / other repo / unreadable →
   `blocked`; the reviewer never runs. A Factory Task can no longer reach
   `merge_ready` with `NO_PR`.
3. `requireNativeReview` defaults to true once a `prBinding` is configured (and
   `relay run factory` sets it explicitly): the independent reviewer must post
   the ISH-883 native `COMMENT` review and Relay must read it back at the
   reviewed head. A local-only structured PASS cannot reach MergeReady.
4. The review body carries the `<!-- ishiul-review head=<sha> verdict=... -->`
   marker **and** `## Findings — attempt <n>` (or `No findings.`), so the
   attempt-N finding text is readable from the PR itself.
5. `confirmMerged` refuses to credit a merge for a code Task with no bound PR
   (`CODE_CHANGE_GATE: NO_PR`). Relay still does not perform merges; a real merge
   is only *observed and credited* against an explicit PR at the recorded head.

## Which reviews count as verdict candidates (ISH-1283)

Relay reads the reviewer's native reviews back with `listReviews` and considers a
review only when ALL of these hold (`verifyNativeReview`,
`src/reviewer-runner.ts:924`):

- authored by the expected `RELAY_REVIEW_AUTHOR` login;
- state `COMMENTED` (PENDING/APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED/DISMISSED never count);
- pinned to the exact reviewed head (`commit_id` matches the task head);
- posted after any base-changed invalidation;
- **body non-empty after trimming** (`isVerdictCandidate`,
  `src/reviewer-runner.ts:909`, applied in the filter at `:956`).

The body check is the ISH-1283 rule. GitHub can record a separate review object
with an empty body when the reviewer submits inline comments after its verdict
review; T407 had the NG marker review at `2026-10-27T08:28:37Z` and an empty-body
review with one inline comment at `08:28:38Z`. An empty body cannot carry the
`ishiul-review` marker, so it is not a verdict candidate and cannot shadow the
verdict. Non-empty prose without a marker **is** a candidate and still fails
closed as `REVIEW_NATIVE_CONTRADICTED`; only a body-less
(inline-comment-only) review is skipped.

The NEWEST candidate is the reviewer's current word at the head. Relay accepts it
only when `reviewBodyHasMarker` (`src/reviewer-runner.ts:976`) matches the
structured verdict and the reviewed head; a later candidate with a different
marker, or a marker naming another head, is `REVIEW_NATIVE_CONTRADICTED` — Relay
never falls back to an older matching review. Reviews pinned to another commit
are still excluded by the unchanged head-pinning rule.

## Provenance rule

The native review / `ishiul-review` marker is posted **only by the reviewer Run**,
never by the Gateway or the coding worker. The GitHub login is shared, so the
provenance guarantee is structural: Relay's only write tool is none; the coding
worker's brief forbids reviews; the reviewer's brief requires one.

## Operator configuration

- **No env is required for the Factory (ISH-1133).** The read-only `gh` reader is
  the default for PR binding and the native review; both legs share one
  detection. `RELAY_PROVIDER_GITHUB=gh` forces it and `off` disables it. When
  unset, the operator/Factory/daemon paths auto-detect a `gh` that passes
  `gh auth status`.
- The Factory authorizes the reviewer's `COMMENT` review by default
  (`RELAY_GITHUB_REVIEW_WRITE=0` opts out and then `requireNativeReview` blocks).
- `RELAY_REVIEW_AUTHOR=<login>` overrides the author; otherwise the authenticated
  `gh api user` login is used.
- The coding binary defaults to `$HOME/.dsh/bin/dsh-model` when executable, else
  `dsh`; `RELAY_DSH_BIN` overrides. The native-review budget defaults to 45 min;
  `RELAY_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides.
- `relay pr bind <task>` / `relay merge-check <task>` print the bound PR
  (`pr=owner/name#n@sha`).

# ISH-1140 — hosted CI is not a merge gate

Status: implemented in Relay (this repo). The ishiul-side gateway/skill text is a
separate change; this document is the contract Relay now enforces.

## Decision (owner, 2026-10-23)

GitHub-hosted CI (Actions check runs and commit statuses) is **not** a merge gate.
`relay merge-check <task>` decides from Relay's own evidence, and must not report
`BLOCKED` because hosted check runs failed or are absent. This closes both live
failures: ishiul PRs whose Actions jobs never start (previously
`BLOCKED — CHECKS_NOT_PASSED` despite green Relay VERIFY) and the relay repo, which
has no hosted CI (previously `BLOCKED — CHECKS_NOT_RUN` on every PR).

## What gates READY

`evaluateMergeGate` (`src/merge-gate.ts:226`) requires all of:

1. a **mechanical VERIFY** result that passed at the Task's recorded head
   (`src/merge-gate.ts:333-345`); missing / failed / another head is
   `VERIFY_MISSING` / `VERIFY_FAILED` / `VERIFY_STALE`;
2. a trusted **independent ReviewResult PASS** pinned to that head
   (`REVIEW_MISSING` / `REVIEW_STALE` / `REVIEW_NOT_INDEPENDENT`), with no
   unresolved `NG` at the head and no owner `HOLD`;
3. an **open, non-draft PR** whose head equals the recorded head and whose base
   branch is the reviewed one, with resolved mergeability (`CONFLICT` raises
   `IntegrationRequired`);
4. **dependencies done** (a PR-bound prerequisite only once merged);
5. a point-of-use **merge authority** (`NO_PERMISSION` otherwise — the gate never
   merges).

## A post-review HEAD move re-enters VERIFY

Because (1) is HEAD-pinned, a moved HEAD must earn a new VERIFY or the Task would
dead-end at `merge_ready`. Every post-review head change goes through
`invalidateReview` (`src/workflow.ts:256-288`): an integration submit or Run that
names a new head (`src/workflow.ts:634-638`, `src/workflow.ts:789-794`) and a
provider-poll PR re-push (`src/workflow.ts:563-566`). On a HEAD change it now
sends the Task back to **`verify`** at the new head and `attempt+1` — with
`claim_role=relay` when the Task has mechanical checks, so
`runPendingMechanicalVerifications` re-runs them; with the Task's own role
otherwise — instead of skipping straight to `review`. A **base-branch** change
keeps the same HEAD, so its VERIFY still applies and only the review re-opens.

`tests/merge-gate.test.ts` covers both paths end to end: integration submit at a
new head -> VERIFY -> review PASS -> integration -> `merge_ready` -> gate
`READY`, and a PR-link head move at `merge_ready` through the same route.

## Hosted CI is informational

Check runs are still read, HEAD-pinned, when a reader is configured

# Task ↔ PR check (ISH-880, read-only as of ISH-885)

Mechanical VERIFY binds a Task's **exact local HEAD**; ISH-761 is a **read-only**
HEAD-bound merge gate. ISH-880 added the one seam that binds a produced commit to
a GitHub PR.
ISH-885 keeps that seam but makes it **read-only**: Relay observes GitHub, it
never writes.

## Who writes GitHub

The GitHub PR workflow is **Agent-owned**:

- the **Coding Agent** (dsh/DeepSeek), in its own Task workspace/checkout, does
  `git commit` + `git push` + `gh pr create`/update with normal credentials;
- the **independent Claude reviewer** posts a native `gh pr review`.

Relay is the supervisor: it owns Task/Run/phase, single-writer, the exact
produced commit, mechanical VERIFY, and the **read-only** Task↔PR check below.
Relay has **no** publisher, no `git push`, no PR mutation and no review
submission. The ISH-880 `GitGhPrPublisher` / `PrPublisher` seam and the
`relay pr bind --publish` / `ProviderAuthority.githubWrite` write path were
**removed** by ISH-885 — they were Agent tools misfiled as Relay capabilities.

### Worker contract (ISH-1087)

The **dsh coding worker**, not the Gateway, opens the PR. The Run brief Relay
pins into the worktree (and passes as the dsh prompt) tells it to:

1. commit, then **push the Task branch** (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`;
   never the default branch);
2. **open the PR while the Run is still live**, before Relay accepts the Run, with
   title **`ISH-<n>: <what changed>`** and a body that follows the target repo's
   `.github/pull_request_template.md`, including a **`## Documentation Impact`**
   section (`None` when there is no docs change);
3. on a FIX, push the new commit to the **same** PR and update its body — never a
   duplicate PR;
4. never merge and never post a review (provenance: the reviewer Run posts the
   verdict).

The brief embeds the target repo's template when it can read it. If the Task
records no `pr_repo`/`pr_url`, Relay resolves `owner/name` from the Task
workspace's `origin` (or the Factory source checkout / `--pr-repo`), so the
instruction is present on the live ishiul intake too.

## Identity is explicit

The Task↔PR identity is a recorded **`pr_url`** (`owner/repo#n`, a GitHub PR URL,
or `#n` with a `pr_repo`). It is **never** inferred from a branch name or output
text alone. The Agent's reported PR URL/SHA are **untrusted claims** until Relay
independently re-reads GitHub. A missing identity is not "no PR" — it is
*unbound*, which can never become a merge-ready PASS.

## The read-only passes

`bindTaskPr(db, taskId, deps)` returns a structured
`PrBindingResult { status, ref, expectedHead, remoteHead, created, reason,
identity }` and, in order:

1. **Recorded identity** — re-read the PR from GitHub and require its `headSha`
   to equal the produced commit (`expectedHead`, default `task.head_sha`). The
   repo, the head repository (never a fork) and the open state are all verified.
2. **Crash-retry adoption** — with no recorded identity, an existing PR on the
   Task's **own repo + branch** is adopted *only when its head equals the
   produced commit* (repo AND head, so this is not branch-name-only inference).
   No duplicate PR is created. A PR that exists at a different head is
   `HEAD_MOVED` (the Agent must push the produced commit to the same PR).
3. **No identity and no adoptable PR** — `NO_PR_IDENTITY`, BLOCKED. Relay does
   **not** publish; the Coding Agent must push and create/update the PR first.

The repo used for passes 1–3 is the Task's `pr_repo`/`pr_url` when recorded,
else the Task workspace's `origin`, else the Factory source checkout. This is
what makes a Task that records only a branch (the live `relay/ish-*` intake)
bindable at all.

Every pass re-reads GitHub and requires the remote head to equal the produced
commit; the recorded `head_sha`/`pr_url` are only written through `linkTask`.

## The legitimate FIX is Agent-owned

When a FIX produces a new commit B, the Agent updates the **same** PR from A to B
and pushes B **first**. Relay then only **observes** B: it re-reads PR #N at B,
compares with the Task's produced B, invalidates A's checks/review and starts a
new-head review. If the PR still shows A while the Task has produced B, Relay
refuses with `HEAD_MOVED` (the Agent has not published yet) rather than
overwriting the remote head itself. If another actor changes the remote HEAD, the
mismatch fails closed too — Relay never overwrites it.

## Fail-closed rules

- A **rate-limited** provider (`PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED`) is typed and retryable:
  it is NOT a "PR unreadable"/"provider not configured" verdict, and binding
  succeeds after the reported reset. A **moved** PR head (`HEAD_MOVED`), an
  **unreadable** provider/PR (`PROVIDER_UNREADABLE`/`PR_UNREADABLE`), a
  **different/fork repo**
  (`REPO_CHANGED` — the PR's head branch must be in the Task's own repo, never a
  fork), a **non-open** PR (`PR_NOT_OPEN`), a **missing/non-full produced commit**
  (`NO_PRODUCED_HEAD`), a caller-supplied head that is not the produced commit
  (`HEAD_MISMATCH`) or no identity/adoptable PR (`NO_PR_IDENTITY`) is **BLOCKED**
  — never a fake `review_pass`, never a silently-accepted stale commit.
- The bound head is the **exact full 40-hex produced commit** (case-insensitive
  equality, never a prefix in either direction) and it is the Task's own
  `head_sha`: a caller-supplied `expectedHead` may only *restate* it, so no input
  can rewrite `task.head_sha` to a commit that was never produced.
- Nothing here pushes, creates/updates a PR, posts a review, merges, approves,
  deletes a branch, or writes Linear.
- A new PR HEAD is VERIFY- and review-invalidating: `reconcileTaskFromProvider`/
  `linkTask` re-enter `verify` at a new attempt when the live PR head moves, so
  old VERIFY/Review evidence at the previous HEAD never carries forward. A
  base-branch retarget keeps the same HEAD and re-opens only the review.

## Factory integration

`FactoryDeps.prBinding` enables the step. When set, the Factory binds **before
the review stage** (at the top of the `review` phase) for every code Task with a
produced commit — including a Task that records only a branch. A BLOCKED bind
returns the Factory outcome `blocked` and the reviewer never runs, so a Factory

# Task Worktree + disposable dsh Run lifecycle (ISH-760)

Relay centrally manages a minimal lifecycle: the **Task / Worktree / branch
persists**, while a **headless dsh Run is disposable** (ISH-803). A coding worker
needs **no Herdr pane, tab, or session attach** — Relay owns the workspace and
launches one process per attempt.

This is implemented in `src/run-lifecycle.ts` on top of the ISH-758 phase machine
(`src/workflow.ts`) and the ISH-803 one-shot runner (`src/dsh-runner.ts`). It does
**not** reimplement either one.

```sh
relay run worktree <task-id> [--branch B] [--base REF] [--path DIR] [--json]
relay run launch   <task-id> [--timeout 30m] [--permission MODE] [--json]
relay run cleanup  <task-id> [--abort REASON] [--apply] [--force] [--repo DIR] [--json]
relay run list     [--task <id>] [--leaks] [--json]          # --leaks = read-only orphan patrol
relay run submit   <run-id> [--evidence E] [--summary S]     # the only thing that advances a Task
```

## One branch + worktree per Task (create / select / own)

`relay run worktree` (or `launch`, which ensures it first) creates, or **selects
and reuses**, the single worktree a Task owns:

- **Branch** — the Task's recorded `branch`, else a deterministic
  `relay/<issue-or-id>[-<slice>]`. Re-running is idempotent; it never mints a
  second branch.
- **Path** — `<control-plane>/worktrees/<task-id>` (under the same `.relay/`
  directory as the DB; never shared `/tmp`).
- **Base** — `--base`, else `task.pr_base`, else `origin/main` when present, else
  `HEAD`.

### Self-contained workspace (ISH-904)

The workspace is a **local clone** of the source repo
(`git clone --local --no-checkout <source> <path>`), not a linked
`git worktree add` checkout. A linked worktree keeps its git dir at
`<source>/.git/worktrees/<T>` and its common dir at `<source>/.git` — both
OUTSIDE the workspace — and a headless Run's default `workspace-write` sandbox
writes only inside its cwd, so every git mutation (`index.lock`, `ORIG_HEAD`,
refs) was denied and the Run could never commit. A local clone has `.git` *inside*
the path, so:

```sh
git -C <path> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir        # <path>/.git
git -C <path> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir # <path>/.git
```

`--local` hardlinks/copies objects (cheap, no network). If the source itself has
`objects/info/alternates` (e.g. a `--shared` clone), the clone would inherit that
escape and read objects outside the workspace, so the alternate objects are
hardlinked into the clone and the alternates file is removed — the workspace is
complete on its own.

`origin` is re-pointed at the **source repo's `origin` URL**
(`git -C <source> remote get-url origin`), so the pinned brief's
`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` pushes to the real provider. A source
with no origin has no provider to push to, so the clone's local-path origin is
**removed** (Relay never invents a remote, and nothing can push into the source
checkout by accident).

Everything else is answered from **local** refs — creating a workspace never
runs `ls-remote`. ISH-904 adds a best-effort `git -C <source> fetch origin`
FIRST (no interactive credentials; a failure is a warning, not a create
failure), so a lane is not cut from a `origin/main` that the last manual fetch
left stale:

- **Base** is resolved in the SOURCE (`git -C <source> rev-parse <base>^{commit}`)
  after that fetch, and that commit is fetched from the source path. This matters
  because the clone's own `refs/remotes/origin/*` are copies of the source's
  **local** branches: left to itself, the default `origin/main` would mean the
  source's local `main`, not the real `refs/remotes/origin/main`. A Task's
  recorded `pr_base` (e.g. `main`) also prefers `origin/<base>`; an explicit
  `--base` is honoured exactly. A resolved base that is behind `origin/main` is
  reported as a binding warning (and in the Factory `steps`), never silently cut.
- **Existing branch** (a re-run/FIX of `relay/<n>`): the source's local branch if
  it has one, else its `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` — a branch that was pushed
  to GitHub but has no local source branch, which a linked `git worktree add` used
  to resolve. It is imported into the clone at the same name (local path fetch).

Consumers that read a produced head from the SOURCE repo (the ISH-829 detached
review worktree) import it first: the source does not share the workspace's
object store, so `importHeadIntoSource` does a local path fetch before
`git worktree add --detach`.

The chosen path + branch are written back to `tasks.worktree` / `tasks.branch`, so
the Task **owns** its workspace. A second call on the same Task returns the
existing binding (`worktree.selected`) instead of creating a new one — this is
what makes a FIX the *same worktree*.

## Pre-launch disk-space guard (ISH-1009)

Before a Run row is inserted, and before `launchTaskRun` creates/pins a
worktree, Relay measures free space on the **worktrees root** and the volume
holding the **Relay DB** (`src/disk-guard.ts`). The threshold is
`RELAY_MIN_FREE_DISK_BYTES` (default 20 GiB; `0` turns off the threshold only —
an unmeasurable volume still refuses). If **either** volume is below it:

- no workspace, Run row, output directory or dsh process is created;
- the Task is left exactly as it was (`queued`), so the next launch attempt
  after space is freed proceeds normally — no manual requeue/unblock;
- a durable `run.launch_refused` event is written with `reason: "low_disk"`,
  `freeBytes`, `minFreeBytes`, the per-path probe results and the launch
  `target`/`scope`;
- `relay status` and the dashboard show the live measurement and the last
  refusal (free space and threshold).

A probe that cannot measure is **not** a pass: the launch is refused with
`reason: "probe_failed"` and the probe error is recorded in the event and
surfaced by both UIs. This is fail-closed by design: an unmeasurable volume is
treated like a full one.

The guard is enforced in `startDshRun` (so raw `relay run start` cannot bypass
it). The Task lifecycle calls the same guard earlier so a low-disk refusal never
creates a worktree.

## The Run brief is pinned BEFORE launch

`launchTaskRun` composes a brief and writes it to
`<worktree>/.relay/run-brief.md` **before** the dsh process starts (the same text
is handed to `dsh --profile headless` and stored as the Run's `spec.md`). The
brief contains:

1. the Task text (ISH-803's `buildTaskPrompt`: title / description / acceptance);
2. the recorded **verification steps** (`--check name=command`);
3. the **prior findings** inherited from the immediately preceding attempt (see
   below).

Pinning into the worktree removes the shared-`/tmp` and late-prompt race: the
worker always sees exactly the durable state Relay had at launch time. `.relay/`
is gitignored, so the brief never appears as a change.

## One disposable Run per phase/attempt; single-writer

`launchTaskRun` launches exactly **one** headless dsh Run (ISH-803's
`startDshRun`) bound at start to Task / phase / attempt / generation / branch /
HEAD, with stdout / stderr / events under `<control-plane>/runs/<run-id>/`.

**Single-writer is enforced in `startDshRun`** (so no entrypoint can bypass it): a
launch is refused with `DUPLICATE_WRITER` while another Run is still
`starting`/`running` on the **same worktree** (resolved path) or the **same
branch**. The existence check and the Run INSERT happen in **one
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction**, so the guard is atomic **across processes** — two
concurrent `relay run launch`/`start` processes cannot both be admitted (the
second blocks/gets `BUSY`, then observes the first committed row and is refused).
A Run's own durable end/cancel row is the confirmation that releases the writer.
Runs in **different** worktrees/branches are allowed to run in parallel, even when
they touch the same files; only when a real conflict appears does the Gateway
decide the fix and Relay re-verifies/re-reviews at the changed HEAD.

`launchTaskRun` also refuses a duplicate writer **before pinning the brief**, so a
launch that will be rejected never writes into the worktree the live Run owns —
the pinned brief always keeps matching the Run that holds the worktree. The atomic
guard inside `startDshRun` remains authoritative.

## Daemon Run liveness sweep (ISH-1008)

The launching coroutine is normally the **only** writer of a Run's terminal row.
If it dies (daemon crash, reboot, or an `ENOSPC` terminal write), the row would
stay `starting`/`running` forever: `DUPLICATE_WRITER` keeps fencing and nobody is
alerted. `reconcile()` therefore runs a throttled liveness pass
(`src/run-liveness.ts`, `RELAY_RUN_LIVENESS_MS` default **45s**) over every
non-terminal Run. The durable throttle advances only after a **clean** pass, so
a write failure (a full disk) retries on the next reconcile tick instead of
waiting a whole interval.

The **launcher** is checked before the dsh. The child can exit while the
launching coroutine still runs `git rev-parse`/`git fetch` before its terminal
write; the Run row records `launcher_pid`/`launcher_lstart`, and the sweep leaves
the row (and the single-writer fence) alone while that launcher may still write.
The lease is cleared in the launcher's `finally`, even when its terminal write
failed, so the next sweep can retry the row.

Local Runs reuse `identifyRunProcess`:

| identity | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `dead` | `failed` (`orphaned: owner pid … is not alive`) |
| `reused` | `failed` (`orphaned: … unrelated process (reused)`); **no signal** |
| `match` | untouched — the writer is live |
| `undeterminable` | untouched — the single-writer fence stays held |

A `starting` row that has not recorded a PID yet is left alone for
`RELAY_RUN_START_GRACE_MS` (default `max(60s, 2 x interval)`), so a sweep never
races a concurrent launch. The sweep never kills a local process: it only writes
a terminal row after proving the original one is gone.

A sweep failure is never a success. It reads the tail of the Run's
`stderr.log`/`dsh.jsonl`, classifies the cause (`ENOSPC`, `OOM`, `signal`,
`unknown`), stores `cause=<CLASS>: <evidence>` in `runs.error`, emits `run.died`,
shows the cause on the dashboard (`RUNS` and `ATTENTION`), and sends immediate
`run_died` mail to the responsible owner. `stderr.log` is authoritative across
all classes; `dsh.jsonl` contributes only its parsed terminal `error` events
(never tool-call output or a success `final` summary), and the last matching line
in a source wins. `relay run show <id>` projects the class as `failure_class`.
When the Run is the one a Factory stop is bound to, `run show`/`run logs` also
project the ISH-1013 `factory` report (classification, cause, evidence and next
action) from the durable `factory.outcome` event; the Run row itself is unchanged.
Per-run errors are isolated so a failed write cannot crash the daemon or prevent
the remaining Runs from being swept. The sweep does **not** add a pre-launch disk
guard (ISH-1009) or stall detection for a live but silent dsh.

## FIX = same worktree + previous findings + a new Run

A review `--fail`/FIX (or a failed mechanical verify) sends the Task back to
`implement` at `attempt+1` (ISH-758), clearing the head. The next `launchTaskRun`:

- reuses the **same** worktree/branch (the Task still owns them);
- computes the **previous findings** from the structured results of the
  immediately preceding attempt (`ReviewResult`/`VerificationResult` with
  `passed=0`) and pins them into the brief — never from another Task, an older
  attempt, or an older HEAD;
- carries the actionable evidence itself: for a VERIFY FAIL, the failing check
  name, outcome, exit code, a bounded/redacted stdout+stderr tail, the verified
  HEAD, the Run's base HEAD and the check's reproduction command (from
  `payload_json.checks`, the existing result); for a REVIEW FIX, the reviewed
  HEAD and the reviewer's `severity`/`file:line`/message findings (the existing
  `reason`); for a **failed IMPLEMENT Run** with no submission (ISH-1012), the
  failed Run id, terminal state/exit code, base + produced HEAD, its recorded
  error and a bounded stderr tail, plus the Factory's bounded-retry reason; in
  all cases the brief still contains the original acceptance;
- labels `not_run`/`inconclusive`/blocked results as **BLOCKED evidence**, not a
  code defect, so they never become a "fix this" instruction. A failed
  IMPLEMENT Run is a **RETRY** instruction only because the Factory already
  classified it as repairable and issued the next attempt; an environment
  failure (ENOSPC/resource/permission/auth/launch) is never retried, so
  the fresh brief never presents it as a code fix;
- starts a **new** disposable dsh Run — there is no session continuation and the
  previous Run is already terminal.

The inherited output is truncated (12 lines / 1200 chars per check) and passed
through the same `redactSecrets` filter as other run evidence; raw logs and
credentials are never copied into the brief.

## A terminal Run CLOSES its attempt (Factory path)

Once an IMPLEMENT Run for `(task, phase=implement, attempt=N)` is terminal it is
**closed** for the Factory: `implementOnce` starts a Run only for a NEW attempt,
and re-entering the Factory with a closed attempt does not start a second writer
for it:

- a clean `exit 0` Run that was never submitted (a crash between the process
  exit and the structured submission) is finished through the ordinary
  `acceptRunSubmission` fence — never re-launched;
- a failed/cancelled/timed-out Run is surfaced as its recorded failure so the
  Factory's bounded-recovery policy decides (new attempt, or an explicit stop);
- `blocked_human` is a **HOLD**: an in-flight Run cannot submit and advance a HELD
  Task, so a late `exit 0` never bypasses the human decision.

## A Run is *not* a submission

`dsh exit 0`, a final assistant message, or an LLM "done" advances **nothing**. The
only path that moves a Task is the structured
`acceptRunSubmission` (`relay run submit`), bound to the current
Task/phase/attempt/**generation**/branch/HEAD. It refuses (never advances):

- a Run that is not a clean `exited`/exit-0 process (failed, signalled, cancelled,
  timeout, still running);
- a Run superseded by a **newer** Run for the same `(task, phase, attempt)` (a late
  event);
- a submission naming a different task/phase/attempt/branch/HEAD, or a **live**
  Task whose head/branch/phase/attempt has moved since the Run started
  (`base_head_sha` is the staleness fence; the Run's own produced `head_sha`, an
  intermediate commit on its history — base ancestor of head ancestor of
  produced — and an own head the worker pushed then **amended/rebased and
  force-pushed away** are accepted because the provider poll may bind the Run's
  own pushed PR head mid-Run, a Run may push more than once between polls, and
  the worker is allowed to amend its own commit — ISH-1125/ISH-1128);
- a duplicate `TaskSubmitted` for the same `(task, phase, attempt)`.

The amended-away head is NOT on the base→produced lineage, so it cannot be
proved by ancestry. While a Run is LIVE, the read-only provider poll records
each PR head it binds in `run_observed_heads` **only when the Run's own
worktree provably held that commit** (current HEAD, or its HEAD reflog) and the
PR is on the Run's own branch. The submit fence accepts a Task head recorded
this way; a head a different writer pushed is never attributed to the Run and
is still refused. A Task with no linked head still adopts the produced head.

The provider poll is bounded (ISH-1132/ISH-1138): it only considers a Task with
a **live Run**, one in `review`/`merge_ready`/`integration`, or a `done` Task
accepted before its bound PR merged (`merged_at IS NULL`, PR not observed
settled). That one terminal candidate is polled until the merge is recorded or a
final `pr_settled_at` observation lands — the PR is closed, or GitHub reports it
merged at a head the Task did not record — then it leaves the poll set for good;
every other terminal `done`/`failed`/`cancelled` Task is never polled. It
spends at most one read per Task per `RELAY_PROVIDER_POLL_MS` (default 60s) —
including the merge gate's HEAD-pinned `check-runs` read. A provider

## Leak patrol (ISH-1221/1222)

`relay run list --leaks` is the read-only patrol the gateway can call. It lists
resources attributable to Relay whose Run/Task is over (or whose Task row is
gone), with sizes:

- per-Run and per-review scratch roots;
- the Task-scoped Cargo build dir (`<worktree>/target`, ISH-1225), reported only
  for a terminal Task with no live writer;
- Task worktrees and disposable review worktrees;
- Relay-labelled containers and volumes (Docker's reported size);
- stopped devcontainer containers whose exact `devcontainer.local_folder` label
  resolves to a Relay-owned worktree/review path of a terminal Task (ISH-1224),
  with Docker's size;
- the exact derived devcontainer `dind-var-lib-docker-*` named volumes, with the
  size Docker reports (`docker system df -v`; rendered `-` when the probe fails).
  An attributed holder is named in the entry (`held by container <id> (name)`),
  including when Docker's `Links` is > 0.

It never lists an unrelated/unrecorded dind volume, any other unlabelled
container/volume, another control plane's `relay.plane` resources, or any image.
Docker being absent/down is reported as `docker unchecked: ...`, not hidden; with
no seam (or `RELAY_DOCKER_RESOURCES=off`) the container/volume section says the
inventory is disabled rather than silently claiming zero. `--json` returns the
same report as structured data.

A dind volume whose holder is NOT attributable (no exact
`devcontainer.local_folder` label on a Relay-owned path) is not reported as
orphaned: stop/remove that container first, then re-run the patrol/cleanup. A dind
volume whose owner Run is finished but whose workspace has a LIVE Run (for
example a FIX attempt reusing the worktree) is never reported (ISH-1224).

A self-contained clone workspace is removed as a directory (`rm -rf`), so the
SOURCE repo's `.git` is never touched (a linked `git worktree remove` would have
mutated it). A legacy linked worktree recorded before ISH-904 is still reclaimed
through `git worktree remove` in its own source. Cleanup is idempotent: a second
`--apply` sees no recorded workspace and is a no-op.

Deleting the directory also deletes the Task branch. A linked worktree left its
branch (and every commit on it) in the source repo, so before removal cleanup
checks whether the workspace holds commits **no remote has**
(`git rev-list <head/branch> --not --remotes`, after refreshing `origin`; an
unreachable remote just keeps the last known tracking state). Those commits are
copied back into the source repo under `refs/relay-kept/<branch>/*` and
`refs/relay-kept/HEAD` (a local path fetch, event `worktree.commits_kept`), which
is the custody the linked worktree used to provide. If the copy fails, removal is
refused. `--force` skips this and really discards the commits.
